title: add
description: `add` builds the new state in one transaction, validates it, then rewrites the files it changed, one write at a time. The rewritten files are what raise `spec:changed`: `lathe serve` watches every product's data folder and Lathe's own (`watchTargets`) and, 150 ms after the last change, sends `spec:changed` to every open page over its event stream. When a write through the MCP server changes a product kind, kind field or relation, the server rereads the schema and sends `notifications/tools/list_changed`.

title: Store.add('check')
description: `add` on `check` builds the new state in one transaction, validates it, refuses a name that one of Lathe's own checks already has (naming `lathe/data/check.jsonl`), then rewrites the product's `check.jsonl` in its data folder. The server watches each product's data folder and `lathe/data` (`watchTargets`), and 150 ms after the last change there sends `spec:changed` to every open page.

title: Store.set('check')
description: `set` on `check`, refusing Lathe's own (`built-in`).

title: Store.remove('check')
description: `remove` on `check`, refusing Lathe's own.

title: Store.set('product_setting')
description: `add` and `set` on `product_setting`, through the store's command layer.

title: navigate
description: `navigate` resolves a `?` patch against the current address (or carries the tools open over the stage to a new path), does nothing when the address would not change, runs the pages' leave-entry notes, then pushes a history entry, or replaces the current one and keeps what was noted in it, and dispatches the `lathe:navigate` event in process; `useLocation` hears it, and `popstate` for Back and Forward, and the page re-renders at the new address.

title: useSpaceState
description: On every page that belongs to a product, `useSpaceState` sets `lathe:space` to that product and stores the page's address, without the tools open over it, as the space's last page in `lathe:space-pages`, skipping the write when nothing changed; choosing a space (`go`) sets `lathe:space` and navigates to its stored page or its product page.

title: SpaceItems.toggle
description: The folders' fold toggles: `toggle` in `SpaceItems` flips a row's entry in `lathe:nav-folders`, opening the branch down to the current page.

title: moveInTab
description: `moveInTab` (app/src/views/tabs.ts, with `movePlace` and `replacePlace` in app/src/views/place.ts), reached through `usePageTabs`' `change`.

title: newTab
description: `newTab` and `duplicateTab` (app/src/views/tabs.ts), reached through `usePageTabs`' `change`.

title: closeTab
description: `closeTab`, reached through `usePageTabs`' `change`.

title: activateTab
description: `activateTab` and `cycleTab`, reached through `usePageTabs`' `change`.

title: updateView
description: `updateView`, reached through `usePageTabs`' `change`: the place's depth, kind filters, wiki card and scroll.

title: useSessionSettings
description: useSessionSettings: the session's settings, and the setters the graph and the wiki card call for the person's own change

title: stepTab
description: `stepTab` (app/src/views/tabs.ts, with `stepPlace` in app/src/views/place.ts), reached through `usePageTabs`' `change` when the window's history steps.

title: usePanelSize.set
description: `usePanelSize`'s setter, `set`, which keeps the size within the panel's limits.

title: toggleNav
description: toggleNav, and the wiki card and stage commands the shell registers

title: choose
description: `choose` in `ThemeProvider` drops any preview and sets `ThemeState.chosen`; the effect that follows applies the theme to the page (`applyTheme`), keeps the state and the theme's stylesheet in local storage (`themeStore.save`), and the window's chrome follows.

title: setMode
description: `setMode` in `ThemeProvider` drops any preview and sets `ThemeState.mode`; the effect that follows applies it to the page (`applyTheme`) and keeps it with the theme's stylesheet in local storage (`themeStore.save`).

title: duplicate
description: `duplicate` in `ThemeProvider` copies the theme's file under a fresh name and ID, records the built-in it came from (`basedOn`), and adds it to `ThemeState.custom` as the chosen theme; the effect that follows keeps it (`themeStore.save`).

title: importFile
description: `importFile` in `ThemeProvider` parses the text as JSON and checks it with `parseTheme`, returning the first error; a valid file gets a fresh name when its own is taken and a new ID, and is added to `ThemeState.custom`, which the effect that follows keeps (`themeStore.save`).

title: update
description: `update` in `ThemeProvider` applies the change to the theme's file and checks the result with `parseTheme`, replacing the theme under the same ID and `basedOn` only when it is valid; it touches only `ThemeState.custom`, which the effect that follows keeps.

title: reset
description: `reset` in `ThemeProvider` finds the built-in theme the copy is based on (Lathe when none is) and `update`s the copy to that theme's file, keeping the copy's name.

title: remove
description: `remove` in `ThemeProvider`: deletes a theme copy.

title: openFolder
description: `openFolder` resolves the path and brings the folder's window forward if one is open. Otherwise it checks the folder (`checkFolder`), showing the reason in a dialog when it fails; once it checks, it adds the folder to the recent folders (`rememberRecent`, `app.addRecentDocument`), opens a hidden window at its saved place (`windowFor`) with the launch view over it, wires the window's save, close and closed handlers, and starts its server (`startApp`), all in the same call.

title: win.on('close')
description: The window's close and closed handlers in `openFolder`: `close` saves the window's bounds, `closed` stops its server and forgets it.

title: saveBounds
description: `saveBounds` reads the window's normal bounds and whether it is maximized or full screen, merges them into the window states by folder (`saveWindow`) and writes window-state.json. It runs 400 ms after a resize, move or full-screen change settles, and as the window closes.

title: applyChrome
description: The `lathe:set-chrome` handler takes the message only from a product window's own page; `applyChrome` checks it is exactly two opaque hex colors (`parseChrome`) and sets the window's background and, off macOS, its controls' overlay. The handler then keeps the colors for the system's light or dark appearance in chrome.json, so new windows open in them.

title: updateBadge
description: The `lathe:error-count` handler, which keeps the window's error count, and `updateBadge`.

title: startServe
description: `startServe` imports the chosen Lathe's `serve()` module and starts it on port 0, trying again (up to five times) when the port it gets is 5199, and throws when the module is not built. In development `startDev` shares the Owner's dev server on 5199 when it serves the folder, else starts a Vite dev server of the shell's own.

title: AppServer.stop
description: Each server's `stop`, from `startServe` or `startDev`.

title: serve
description: `serve` throws when the built app is missing, watches the data folders (`watchTargets`) and sends each change to the open event streams 150 ms after it settles, answers `/api/` paths through `handleApi` and serves the app's files, falling back to index.html. Its stop closes the watchers and connections, waits for the requests in progress, then closes the stores and the engine.

title: addRecent
description: `addRecent` puts the resolved path first, drops any other spelling of it from the list and cuts the list to `RECENT_LIMIT`; it is a pure function, and `rememberRecent` writes its result to recent-folders.json and rebuilds the menu.

title: clearRecent
description: `clearRecent` in `refreshMenu`: clears the system's recent documents and remembers an empty list.

title: initProduct
description: `initProduct` checks `--name` and `--prefix` (capital letters and digits, starting with a letter), writes `lathe.config.json` with this Lathe's schema version and `data` when the repo has none, then opens the store and adds the product, refusing a product that already exists. `lathe/bin/lathe.ts` prints what it wrote, or the refusal.

title: optOutOfWindowRestoration
description: The window restoration opt-out, `optOutOfWindowRestoration`: sets ApplePersistenceIgnoreState and NSQuitAlwaysKeepsWindows on macOS, and nothing elsewhere.

title: readOverrides
description: readOverrides and resolveCommands: unknown commands, bad values and browser essentials dropped.

title: upgradeProduct
description: `upgradeProduct` refuses a git working tree with changes, or no git, and a missing converter (`readConverters`), runs every converter on the raw rows, then opens the store, which runs every aggregate's rules, and rewrites the touched tables in its order; only then does it write the new schema version to the config. When the data does not load, it stops with the reasons as to-dos.

title: mcp-server.mjs
description: The launcher, with installedLathe, versionWarning and warnOnce in lathe-root.mjs

title: openChat
description: Finds the user's `claude`, reads the saved transcript, gives the CLI the window's app bridge, and starts a ChatSession.

title: send
description: ChatSession.send: adds the message to the chat and writes it to the CLI.

title: answer
description: ChatSession.answer: writes the control response and records the answer on the prompt.

title: stop
description: ChatSession.stop: writes the interrupt and marks the chat stopping until the turn's result.

title: openAnswer
description: Navigates the window to the record's address and says what it opened; callAppTool (lathe/src/cli/app-tools.ts), which the MCP server and `lathe app open` share, reaches it through the bridge (desktop/src/bridge.ts).

title: Store.link('follows')
description: `link` on `follows`, through the store's command layer.

title: Store.set('setting_value')
description: `add` and `set` on `setting_value`, through the store's command layer.
